changes_vs_current: Method: 13 people sources (7 general villain polls/search studies + 5 horror-only + 1 Disney-only), average position with missing = list length + 5, ties by source count. Computed order: 1 Hannibal 4.31 (10 sources), 2 Joker 6.69, 3 Vader 7.27, 4 Freddy 9.46, 5 Bates 10.19, 6 Voldemort 10.38, 7 Thanos 10.42, 8 Chucky 10.50, 9 Michael Myers 10.65, 10 Pennywise 10.96, 11 Terminator 11.08, 12 Scar 11.15, 13 Gruber 11.38, 14 Landa 11.50, 15 Kylo Ren 11.54, 16 Queen of Hearts 11.81, 17 Bane 11.92, 18 Amon Goeth 12.04, 19 Alien 12.15, 20-24 Cruella/Maleficent/Tyler Durden/Alonzo Harris/Calvin Candie 12.19 (1 source each), 25 Jack Torrance 12.23 (3 sources), 26 Ratched 12.31, 27 Chigurh 12.38, 28 Leatherface 12.38, 29 Loki 12.54, 30 Jason 12.54, 33 Wicked Witch 12.62. (General sources alone give Hannibal, Joker, Vader, Voldemort, Thanos, Bates, Terminator, Gruber, Landa, Kylo.) Judgment moves: (1) Vader 3 -> 1, Hannibal 1 -> 3: Hannibal's lead comes from UK/Irish polls and horror 'scary' surveys that Vader isn't eligible for. The US sources put Vader first: Fandango US fan vote #1, NBC bracket champion over Hannibal, THR industry #1, plus Empire readers #1. Joker stays 2. (2) Voldemort, Thanos and Michael Myers go ahead of Bates and Chucky (5-9 are within 0.5 of each other). Bates's lift comes from a 2001 web poll and a 2018 state-count study; the gut check has Voldemort/Myers/Thanos. (3) Wicked Witch 33 -> 13 (gut check): Fandango US #9, THR industry #3, Ipsos Canada 2012 most-cited villain. It stays just outside the top 12 because the UK, Empire and global-search top 10s leave it out. (4) Jason Voorhees 30 -> 14 (gut check): tied #1 on US Twitter state counts, #2 in the heart-rate study, made the NBC bracket. Not higher, because Fandango's US top 15 leaves him out while Freddy and Myers make it. (5) Gruber 13 -> 15, Landa 14 -> 16, Kylo 15 -> 17, Queen of Hearts 16 -> 19, Bane 17 -> 18, Goeth 18 -> 20, Alien 19 -> 21, Cruella 20 -> 22, Maleficent 21 -> 23 all shift down only to make room for those two moves. Bane goes ahead of Queen of Hearts because the JoBlo tie-break has Queen of Hearts at 1%. (6) 20-25 tie band (12.19-12.23): Cruella and Maleficent beat Durden/Alonzo/Candie on the JoBlo tie-break and on Shane's Disney map. Jack Torrance (3 sources: UK poll #9, Plex 31%, Frontier top 5) takes #24 over three single-source Shane entries. Versus the current list: Vader 1 and Joker 2 unchanged. Hannibal 3 unchanged. Voldemort 4 -> 5. Gruber 5 -> 15 (only 3 general polls, missing from all US search and horror data). Freddy 6 -> 4 (Fandango #5, #1 in Morning Consult and Plex US polls). Thanos 7 -> 6. Myers 8 -> 7. Terminator 9 -> 11. Loki 10 -> out (Empire-reader artifact, 1 source, computed 29). Wicked Witch 11 -> 13. Landa 12 -> 16. Bates 13 -> 8 (5 sources). Kylo 14 -> 17. Pennywise 15 -> 10 (Fandango, YouGov GB 19%, Twitter state ties). Agent Smith 16 -> out (Fandango only). Chigurh 17 -> out (computed 27). Ratched 18 -> out (computed 26). Sauron 19 -> out (Fandango #15 only). Alien 20 -> 21. Scar 21 -> 15 (Shane Disney #1, Mental Floss 2025 Disney #1, gut check). Queen of Hearts 22 -> 19. Bane 23 -> 18. Cruella 24 -> 22. New entries: Chucky 9 (5 sources incl. Morning Consult 54%, Plex 39%), Jason 14, Amon Goeth 20 (UK poll #8 + Shane 2 states), Maleficent 23, Jack Torrance 24. Aliases from the current list are kept; new aliases are checked for collisions (no bare 'hans', 'it' or 'witch').
confidence: medium for 1-4 (Vader/Joker/Hannibal at the top in every general source; Freddy strong in US horror polls), medium-low for 5-14, low for 15-24. There is still no representative US poll asking for favorite movie villain overall. The general sources are fan votes (Fandango US, Empire, TheJournal), a UK survey and search-data studies. Horror-only and Disney-only sources lift genre villains, and that is a judgment call. 15-24 are near-ties (11.4-12.2) mostly decided by state-count search studies. YouGov Ratings has no fictional-character category reachable (404), IMDb and Ranker were blocked (403/401), Rolling Stone readers' poll paywalled, Wikipedia pageviews rate-limited, so none are cited. Every spot has at least 1 people source; all top-10 items have 3+.
